q: Oxidation numbers have a variety of uses in chemistry, from writing formulae to predicting properties of compounds and assisting in the _____ of oxidation-reduction reactions.
e: Oxidation numbers assist in the balancing of oxidation-reduction reactions in which electrons are transferred.

q: The oxidation number (or oxidation state) of an atom can be _____.
e: The oxidation number of an atom can be zero, positive, or negative.

q: All elements in their free state (uncombined with other elements) have an oxidation number of _____.
e: All elements in their free state have an oxidation number of zero.

q: A positive oxidation number means the atom has _____ electrons assigned to it than in the neutral atom.
e: A positive oxidation number means the atom has fewer electrons assigned to it than in the neutral atom.

q: A negative oxidation number means the atom has _____ electrons assigned to it than in the neutral atom.
e: A negative oxidation number means the atom has more electrons assigned to it than in the neutral atom.

q: The oxidation number of an atom that has lost or gained electrons to form an ion is the same as the _____ of the ion.
e: The oxidation number of an ion is the same as the positive or negative charge of the ion.

q: All elements regardless of whether they are monoatomic, diatomic or triatomic have an oxidation number of _____.
e: All elements regardless of atomicity have an oxidation number of zero in their free state.

q: The algebraic sum of the oxidation numbers of the atoms in a neutral molecule is _____.
e: The algebraic sum of the oxidation numbers of the atoms in a neutral molecule is zero.

q: The algebraic sum of the oxidation numbers of the atoms in a polyatomic ion is equal to the _____ on the ion.
e: The algebraic sum of the oxidation numbers in a polyatomic ion equals the charge on the ion.

q: The oxidation number of H is +1, except in metal hydrides, where it is _____.
e: In metal hydrides like $NaH$, $LiH$, or $CaH_2$, the oxidation number of H is -1.

q: The oxidation number of O is -2, except in peroxides, where it is _____.
e: In peroxides such as $H_2O_2$, $BaO_2$, or $Na_2O_2$, the oxidation number of O is -1.

q: The oxidation number of O is +2 in the compound _____.
e: In $OF_2$, fluorine is more electronegative, making the oxidation number of O +2.

q: Alkali metals in combined state have an oxidation number of _____.
e: Alkali metals in a combined state always have an oxidation number of +1.

q: Alkaline earth metals in combined state have an oxidation number of _____.
e: Alkaline earth metals in a combined state always have an oxidation number of +2.

q: The oxidation number of halogen in compounds (e.g., $BaCl_2$, $NaBr$, $KI$) is typically _____.
e: The oxidation number of halogen in standard compounds is -1.

q: In interhalogen compounds (e.g., $BrF$, $IF_7$, $ClF_3$), the oxidation number of halogen is _____.
e: In interhalogen compounds and compounds like $KClO_3$, the oxidation number of halogen is positive.

q: In covalent compounds, the negative oxidation number is assigned to the _____ atom.
e: In covalent compounds, the negative oxidation number is assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: The oxidation number of sulphur in sulphuric acid ($H_2SO_4$) is _____.
e: In $H_2SO_4$, the oxidation number of sulphur is calculated to be +6.

q: The oxidation number of manganese in the permanganate ion ($MnO_4^-$) is _____.
e: In the permanganate ion ($MnO_4^-$), the oxidation number of manganese is +7.

q: A positive oxidation number indicates the number of electrons _____ from a neutral atom.
e: A positive oxidation number indicates the number of electrons removed from a neutral atom.

q: A negative oxidation number indicates the number of electrons _____ to a neutral atom.
e: A negative oxidation number indicates the number of electrons added to a neutral atom.

q: In $NaCl$, the oxidation number for the $Na^+$ ion is _____.
e: The $Na^+$ ion has one less electron than the neutral Na atom, giving it an oxidation number of +1.

q: In $LiH$, the oxidation number of H is _____.
e: $LiH$ is a metal hydride, so the oxidation number of H is -1.

q: In $BaO_2$, the oxidation number of O is _____.
e: $BaO_2$ is a peroxide, so the oxidation number of O is -1.

q: The metallic element in an ionic compound has a _____ oxidation number.
e: The metallic element in an ionic compound has a positive oxidation number.

q: When a substance gains oxygen in a chemical reaction, it is _____.
e: When a substance gains oxygen in a chemical reaction, it is oxidised.

q: When a substance loses oxygen in a chemical reaction, it is _____.
e: When a substance loses oxygen in a chemical reaction, it is reduced.

q: When a substance loses hydrogen in a chemical reaction, it is _____.
e: When a substance loses hydrogen in a chemical reaction, it is oxidised.

q: When a substance gains hydrogen in a chemical reaction, it is _____.
e: When a substance gains hydrogen in a chemical reaction, it is reduced.

q: Oxidation is the addition of oxygen (or _____ element) to a substance.
e: Oxidation is the addition of oxygen or an electronegative element to a substance.

q: Reduction is the removal of oxygen (or _____ element) from a substance.
e: Reduction is the removal of oxygen or an electronegative element from a substance.

q: Oxidation is the removal of hydrogen (or _____ element) from a substance.
e: Oxidation is the removal of hydrogen or an electropositive element from a substance.

q: Reduction is the addition of hydrogen (or _____ element) to a substance.
e: Reduction is the addition of hydrogen or an electropositive element to a substance.

q: Oxidation is the _____ of electrons by an element, compound or ion.
e: Oxidation is defined as the loss of electrons by an element, compound, or ion.

q: Reduction is the _____ of electrons by an element, compound or ion.
e: Reduction is defined as the gain of electrons by an element, compound, or ion.

q: Any element which _____ in oxidation number is said to be oxidised.
e: Any element which increases in oxidation number is said to be oxidised.

q: Any element which _____ in oxidation number is said to be reduced.
e: Any element which decreases in oxidation number is said to be reduced.

q: In the reaction $N_2(g) + O_2(g) ightarrow 2NO(g)$, nitrogen is _____ because it gains oxygen.
e: Nitrogen gains oxygen in this reaction, so it is oxidised.

q: When copper(II) oxide reacts with coke at high temperature, copper(II) oxide has been _____ to copper because it loses oxygen.
e: Copper(II) oxide loses oxygen, so it is reduced to copper.

q: In the reaction $Cl_2(g) + H_2S(g) ightarrow S(s) + 2HCl(g)$, hydrogen sulphide loses hydrogen and it is _____.
e: Hydrogen sulphide loses hydrogen, so it is oxidised.

q: In the reaction $H_2(g) + Cl_2(g) ightarrow 2HCl(g)$, chlorine gains hydrogen and it is _____.
e: Chlorine gains hydrogen in this reaction, so it is reduced.

q: Oxygen belongs to a class of _____ elements.
e: Oxygen belongs to a class of electronegative elements.

q: Hydrogen belongs to a class of _____ elements.
e: Hydrogen belongs to a class of electropositive elements.

q: In the reaction $Zn(s) + Cu^{2+}(aq) ightarrow Zn^{2+}(aq) + Cu(s)$, zinc is _____ due to the loss of two electrons.
e: Zinc loses electrons, so it is oxidised.

q: In the reaction $Zn(s) + Cu^{2+}(aq) ightarrow Zn^{2+}(aq) + Cu(s)$, the copper(II) ion is _____ due to the gain of two electrons.
e: The copper(II) ion gains electrons, so it is reduced.

q: In the reaction $P_4 + 5O_2 + 6H_2O ightarrow 4H_3PO_4$, the oxidation number of phosphorus increases from 0 to _____, therefore P has been oxidised.
e: The oxidation number of phosphorus increases from 0 to +5, so it is oxidised.

q: In the reaction $P_4 + 5O_2 + 6H_2O ightarrow 4H_3PO_4$, the oxidation number of oxygen is decreased from 0 to _____, therefore oxygen has been reduced.
e: The oxidation number of oxygen decreases from 0 to -2, so it is reduced.

q: Chemical reactions which involve oxidation as well as reduction processes simultaneously, are known as _____ reactions.
e: Reactions involving simultaneous oxidation and reduction are known as redox reactions.

q: The separate oxidation and reduction reactions are called _____.
e: The separate oxidation and reduction reactions are called half-reactions.

q: Redox reactions require a track of each _____ to each atom in chemical reactions.
e: Redox reactions require a track of each electron to each atom in chemical reactions.

q: In living things, the redox reaction that provides food for the plant is _____.
e: Photosynthesis is a redox reaction that provides food for the plant.

q: In living things, the redox reaction that keeps you alive is _____.
e: Respiration is a redox reaction that keeps you alive.

q: In the combustion of magnesium ribbon, magnesium loses electrons and so it is _____.
e: Magnesium loses electrons, so it is oxidised.

q: In the combustion of magnesium ribbon, oxygen gains electrons and so it is _____.
e: Oxygen gains electrons, so it is reduced.

q: The reaction between magnesium and oxygen is a _____ reaction.
e: The reaction between magnesium and oxygen is a redox reaction.

q: An oxidising agent or oxidant is an _____ of electrons and is reduced itself in a chemical reaction.
e: An oxidising agent is an acceptor of electrons and is reduced itself.

q: The oxidising agent is normally in one of its _____ possible oxidation states because it will gain electrons and be reduced.
e: The oxidising agent is normally in one of its higher possible oxidation states.

q: A reducing agent or reductant is a _____ of electrons and is oxidised itself in a chemical reaction.
e: A reducing agent is a donor of electrons and is oxidised itself.

q: The reducing agent is typically in one of its _____ possible oxidation states because it will lose electrons and be oxidised.
e: The reducing agent is typically in one of its lower possible oxidation states.

q: Examples of oxidising agents include oxygen, halogens, concentrated sulphuric acid, nitric acid, hydrogen peroxide, potassium permanganate, potassium dichromate, and _____.
e: Metallic oxides are examples of oxidising agents.

q: Examples of reducing agents include carbon, carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide, hydrogen, hydrogen sulphide, and _____.
e: Metals are examples of reducing agents.

q: In the reaction between magnesium and copper(II) oxide, copper(II) oxide is reduced by gaining electrons from magnesium, so copper(II) oxide is an _____.
e: Copper(II) oxide accepts electrons and is reduced, making it an oxidising agent.

q: In the reaction between magnesium and copper(II) oxide, magnesium causes the reduction of copper(II) oxide by losing electrons, therefore magnesium is a _____.
e: Magnesium donates electrons and is oxidised, making it a reducing agent.

q: The oxidising agent helps the other substance to get _____, and it gets reduced.
e: The oxidising agent helps the other substance to get oxidised.

q: The reducing agent helps the other substance to get _____, and it gets oxidised.
e: The reducing agent helps the other substance to get reduced.

q: One way to balance oxidation-reduction equations is by keeping track of the electron transfer using the _____ of each of the atoms.
e: Balancing redox equations can be done by tracking electron transfer using oxidation numbers.

q: The _____ chemical equation is the most important criterion for solving any stoichiometry problem.
e: The balanced chemical equation is the most important criterion for solving stoichiometry problems.

q: When balancing ionic redox equations using half-equations, balance the oxygen atoms by adding _____.
e: Oxygen atoms are balanced by adding water molecules.

q: When balancing ionic redox equations in acidic conditions, balance the hydrogen atoms by adding _____.
e: In acidic conditions, hydrogen atoms are balanced by adding $H^+$ ions.

q: In the half-equation method, balance the charge of each chemical equation with _____.
e: The charge of each half-equation is balanced with electrons.

q: When balancing a redox reaction in alkaline condition, add _____ to each side of the net reaction to balance any $H^+$.
e: In alkaline conditions, hydroxide ions ($OH^-$) are added to balance $H^+$.

q: In alkaline conditions, $OH^-$ and $H^+$ ions on the same side of a reaction should be added together to form _____.
e: $OH^-$ and $H^+$ ions on the same side combine to form water.

q: In balancing redox equations using oxidation numbers, a change in oxidation number represents the number of _____ transferred.
e: A change in oxidation number represents the number of electrons transferred.

q: When balancing redox equations using oxidation numbers, multiply appropriate coefficients to make the total increase in oxidation number equal to the total _____ in oxidation number.
e: The total increase in oxidation number must equal the total decrease.

q: In balancing redox equations, adjust the coefficients as necessary to give the correct numbers of _____ in the final step.
e: Coefficients are adjusted to give the correct numbers of atoms.

q: When balancing ionic redox equations using half-equations, first balance the number of atoms of the elements other than _____ and _____.
e: Atoms other than O and H are balanced first in the half-equation method.

q: In the half-equation method, if the electrons on each side are not equal, they must be multiplied by appropriate _____.
e: Electrons must be multiplied by appropriate integers to make them equal on both sides.

q: When adding half-equations, cancelling out the _____ forms one balanced chemical equation.
e: Cancelling out the electrons forms one balanced chemical equation.

q: An acidic condition usually implies a solution with an excess of _____ concentration.
e: An acidic condition implies a solution with an excess of $H^+$ concentration.

q: Balancing a redox reaction in basic condition requires the addition of _____ ions.
e: Balancing in basic condition requires the addition of $OH^-$ ions.

q: The oxidation of fuels such as petrol, gas, wood, etc. produces a large amount of _____ which we need for various purposes in daily life.
e: Oxidation of fuels produces a large amount of energy.

q: Oxidation of food in the digestive system causes the changes in proteins and nutrients required for _____ reactions.
e: Oxidation of food causes changes required for biochemical reactions.

q: Oxidation of fats and oils lead to _____.
e: Oxidation of fats and oils leads to rancidity.

q: In fruits such as apples, oxidation can result in the formation of compounds which change the _____ of fruit.
e: Oxidation in fruits can result in compounds which change the colour of the fruit.

q: Margarine and other butter substitutes are produced by using _____ of oils from corn, peanuts and soybeans.
e: Margarine is produced by using reduction of oils.

q: Breathalysers, to estimate the content of alcohol in drivers' breathes, employ the chemical principle of _____ reaction.
e: Breathalysers employ the chemical principle of redox reaction.

q: Oxidising and reducing agents are used in industrial applications such as purifying water, bleaching fabrics, and storing energy in _____ and fuel cells.
e: Oxidising and reducing agents are used in storing energy in batteries and fuel cells.
